paper_title: PELMS Pre-training for Effective Low-Shot Multi-Document Summarization
caption: Low-shot pre-trained model performance on the multi-document summarization (MDS) task with ROUGE-G scores (geometric mean of ROUGE-1/2/L) aggregated over 6 MDS benchmarks. We compare with fully-supervised training (solid lines) and with adapter training (dashed lines) where only 5% of model parameters are tuned. achieves stronger overall performance at all data quantities and training methods when compared to competitive long-input summarization models.

annotations.annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of training examples and the overall ROUGE-G score across different models and conditions. The x-axis is labeled "# Training Examples" and uses an exponential scale ranging from 0 to 64, with tick intervals at 0, 16, and 64. The y-axis is labeled "Overall ROUGE-G Score," also on a linear scale, ranging from 11.0 to 19.0 with tick intervals at 13.0, 15.0, 17.0, and 19.0. The solid green line with circle markers represents the "PELMS" model, starting at a score of 17.0 at 0 training examples and ending at approximately 18.8 at 64. The dashed green line with circle markers, representing "PELMS (5%)," starts at slightly below 17.0 and ends near 18.0. The solid blue line with triangle markers shows the "Pegasus-X" model, beginning at about 13.4 and rising to 18.0, while the dashed blue line, "Pegasus-X (5%)", starts slightly above 13.5 and ends at approximately 14. The solid red line with square markers for the "Primera" model starts at 15 and ends slightly above 18.0. Meanwhile, the dashed red line, "Primera (5%)," begins at 15.0 and maintains a steady trend, also ending slightly above 16.0. The solid yellow line with diamond markers for "Centrum" begins at 16 and ends near 16.3, while the dashed yellow line, "Centrum (5%)," starts just below 16 and finishes slightly below 16, showing a nearly flat trend across the x-axis. The red solid line intersect the green dashed line at x -value of 16. All the line styles can be matched to labels using the legend below the plot.
